summary: Authors may use AI tools only with human oversight and must declare their use in a dedicated statement placed before the reference list at submission. Basic tools such as grammar, spelling and reference checkers and accessibility-only assistive tools need no declaration. AI cannot be listed as an author, and AI may not create or alter primary research images. Editors and reviewers may not upload unpublished manuscripts into generative AI tools, but may use AI in a supportive capacity to improve language or run background literature searches.

evidence.quote: Authors preparing a manuscript for this journal may use AI tools to support them.
AI tools may only be applied with human oversight and control.
Authors must declare the use of generative AI tools in the manuscript preparation process upon submission of the paper.
The declaration does not apply to the use of basic tools, such as tools used to check grammar, spelling, and references.
authors must not list or cite AI tools as an author or co-author on the manuscript
AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data
AI tools may be used to support the creation of explanatory images (such as flow charts, conceptual diagrams, or schematic illustrations).
AI tools may be used in a supportive capacity by editors and reviewers to improve structure and language of the review report
this journal does not currently allow academic editors and reviewers to upload an unpublished manuscript into a generative AI tool
AI tools may be used in a supportive capacity by editors and reviewers to improve structure and language of the review report or editorial decision letter
